lyrics:
[Intro: soft piano, a hospital monitor beeping in time]

[Chorus: female voice, tender]
Save me a chair, I'm on my way
Don't you go anywhere today
I know it's dark, I know you're scared
Hold on tight, save me a chair

[Verse 1: male rap, urgent, tender]
Got your text at a red light, ran it, I'm sorry
Fourth floor, room nine, I know the way, don't worry
You were the one who taught me how to ride a bike, to fight
To tie a hook, to pray at night
Now there's tubes and there's numbers and a doctor who won't guess
And you're cracking jokes like always, like you ain't a mess
I'm twenty minutes out, doing ninety, I'm a wreck
I got one prayer left and I ain't used it yet

[Chorus: female voice, tender, beat fuller]
Save me a chair, I'm on my way
Don't you go anywhere today
I know it's dark, I know you're scared
Hold on tight, save me a chair

[Verse 2: rap, slower, quieter]
Walked in, and there's somebody already by the bed
I can't see him. I can tell. It's the way you tilt your head
You said, "He's been here all night. He don't sleep. He don't leave.
He knows about hospitals. He knows about grief."
He raised a little girl up off a bed just like this one
He cried outside a tomb before he called his friend to come
He took the worst there is and walked out the other side
So whichever way this goes tonight, it's him you're beside

[Bridge: female voice, piano only]
"I'll save you a chair. I've gone ahead.
I've got a place for you," he said.
"In my Father's house there's room to spare.
Either side of the river, I'll be there."

[Final Chorus: both voices, strings]
Save me a chair, I'm on my way
Jesus, stay with him today
I know it's dark, I know we're scared
Hold on tight, save me a chair

[Outro: piano, the monitor steady, spoken]
Hey. You came.
Course I came.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, F minor. Slow, tense and tender, a ballad with a hip-hop pulse.

VOICE: A woman with a clear, soulful voice sings the chorus and the bridge softly, with small gospel turns. A man raps the verses: fast and breathless in verse 1, slow and hushed in verse 2. They sing the last chorus together. Two spoken lines at the end, the first in an older, weak voice.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, a hospital monitor beep used as a metronome, a deep 808 bass, slow trap hi-hats and a soft snare, a string quartet from the bridge, a warm pad.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and monitor. 0:10 Chorus 1. 0:34 Verse 1, the drive. 1:02 Chorus 2. 1:20 Verse 2, the visitor. 1:54 Bridge, his promise. 2:22 Final chorus with strings. 2:50 Outro, piano, the steady monitor and two spoken lines, ends 3:26.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2010s pop-rap ballad: clean, spacious, piano and vocals close, low end deep and soft.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I can't see him. I can tell.' at 1:26.

THE REVEAL: The first eighty seconds are a man racing to a bedside. Verse 2 at 1:20 finds an unseen visitor already there, described through Jairus's daughter, Lazarus and the resurrection. The bridge is his promise from John 14, and the last chorus prays to him by name.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Panic, arrival, awe, peace whichever way it goes.
